findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of flag state
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then always returns `false` in both branches (if enabled, return false; otherwise fall through to return false). This means the function is dead/confusing code that always disables SQL expressions no matter the feature flag state. While the net effect (always disabled) achieves the security goal of this PR, the logic is misleading and buggy — if someone later tries to re-enable the feature by flipping the flag, it will silently not work, and the variable `enabled` is unused in a meaningful way. This should be simplified to `return false` directly with a comment, to avoid confusion and dead code since the flag check is a no-op.

findings.title: TablesList still calls RunCommands which always errors
findings.body: TablesList() calls duckDB.RunCommands(...) against the new stub DB in db.go, which unconditionally returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. Combined with reader.go's always-false enable check, SQL expressions are effectively disabled, but this leaves two different disablement mechanisms (feature flag always false, and stub DB always erroring) that could get out of sync if one is fixed without the other, potentially creating confusing behavior or partial re-enablement bugs in the future.

findings.title: Unused parameters in stub methods not referenced, could trigger lint warnings
findings.body: The stub methods in db.go (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) take parameters that are never used in the function bodies. While harmless at runtime, this can trigger unused-parameter lint warnings and signals that this is dead placeholder code; a comment explaining the stub's purpose (and that it intentionally disables SQL expressions) would help future maintainers understand why DB does nothing instead of assuming it's an incomplete implementation.

findings.title: No test coverage asserting SQL expressions are disabled
findings.body: The PR's stated purpose is to disable SQL expressions to prevent an RCE/LFI vulnerability, but no test was added to pkg/expr (e.g., in reader_test.go or sql_command_test.go) that verifies QueryTypeSQL requests are rejected with the expected error, or that NewSQLCommand/Execute paths fail safely when the feature is toggled on. Given the security-critical nature of this change, a regression test ensuring the vulnerability can't be silently reintroduced is important and currently missing.
